report.summary: Analyzed chunk 5 of ledger.py: defines _resolve, _append_event, _terminal_event, get, open_intents, recent_intents, intents_matching_payload.
risks: _resolve | high | canonical_json(detail) called before transaction; if it raises, detail is not serialized but lock is not acquired. That is intentional per comment. | Confirm that canonical_json does not have side effects.
_resolve | medium | Raises UnknownIntent or IntentAlreadyResolved; callers must handle these. | Check if exceptions are documented.
open_intents | medium | Returns list of Intent with state=STATE_INTENDED; assumes no terminal event exists. | Verify that _row_to_intent works with state parameter.
recent_intents | low | Non-positive limit returns empty list; comment says 'truthful answer'. | Confirm behavior matches expectation.
intents_matching_payload | medium | Substring match on TEXT; relies on canonical_json format. | If payload format changes, matching may break.
intents_matching_payload | low | LIKE metacharacters are escaped; not shown in code. | Verify escaping logic elsewhere.
todos: Review intents_matching_payload for escaping of LIKE metacharacters.
Ensure canonical_json is imported and functional.

handoff.purpose: Defines resolution logic, terminal event detection, and read methods for intents.

symbols.name: _resolve
symbols.note: Resolves an intent by appending an event; raises if unknown or already resolved.

symbols.name: _append_event
symbols.note: Inserts a row into intent_events; returns lastrowid.

symbols.name: _terminal_event
symbols.note: Fetches the latest terminal event (COMPLETED or FAILED) for an intent.

symbols.name: get
symbols.note: Returns an Intent by id, or None.

symbols.name: open_intents
symbols.note: Returns intents with no terminal event, oldest first; used as crash-recovery worklist.

symbols.name: recent_intents
symbols.note: Returns all intents, newest first, with optional kind filter and limit.

symbols.name: intents_matching_payload
symbols.note: Returns intents whose payload contains a key-value pair; substring match.

claims.text: canonical_json before opening the transaction: an unserialisable result must fail without leaving a half-open write lock.
claims.why: The code calls canonical_json(detail) before entering the with self._txn() block, so if it raises, no transaction is opened.

claims.text: resolution is once-only, so a second state is refused rather than silently absorbed
claims.why: The code checks if a prior terminal event exists and raises IntentAlreadyResolved if so.

claims.text: open_intents is the crash-recovery worklist: anything here either never had its effect performed, or had it performed and lost the acknowledgement
claims.why: The docstring describes semantics that depend on external usage; the code only returns intents without terminal events.

claims.text: recent_intents is the read that closes the loop's return path
claims.why: This describes intended usage outside the code chunk.

claims.text: Without it the picker re-selects the same candidate forever (measured: five recorded gate-failed attempts left the top five of the queue unchanged).
claims.why: Refers to external behavior not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: Newest first because every caller wants recency; limit is applied in SQL so a long-lived ledger does not have to be hydrated in full
claims.why: SQL orders by id DESC and uses LIMIT clause when limit is provided.

claims.text: A non-positive limit returns nothing, which is the truthful answer to 'give me zero rows' and keeps a caller's arithmetic (limit=n-1) from silently meaning 'all'.
claims.why: Code returns [] if limit is not None and int(limit) <= 0.

claims.text: A row limit is a WINDOW, not a bound: with it, the oldest attempts silently fall out of memory and their tasks become selectable again
claims.why: Describes behavior of a hypothetical limit-based approach, not present in this code.

claims.text: Matching is a substring test against the payload TEXT, which is exact here rather than approximate because every payload is written through canonical_json: sorted keys, no whitespace, ensure_ascii. So a recorded key/value pair always appears verbatim as 'key':'value'.
claims.why: The substring matching logic is not shown in this chunk; only the filtering of empty values is present.

claims.text: LIKE metacharacters in either are escaped, so a value containing % matches only a literal %.
claims.why: Escaping logic is not shown in this chunk; only value filtering is present.

observations.what: _resolve calls canonical_json(detail) before the transaction, ensuring serialization failure does not leave a half-open lock.
_resolve raises UnknownIntent if row is None, and IntentAlreadyResolved if a terminal event exists.
open_intents uses NOT EXISTS with STATE_COMPLETED and STATE_FAILED to find intents without terminal events.
recent_intents returns [] for non-positive limit, as documented.
intents_matching_payload filters out empty strings from values list but does not show the actual matching logic.
